text:
CLion C/C++ IDE with CMake & Debugger for Windows 11

 

 🚀 PowerShell Quick Install

 

 

 

---

CLion is a professional-grade integrated development environment engineered for C and C++ workflows, delivering intelligent code completion, real-time static analysis, and integrated CMake support within a unified desktop workspace. The environment provides deep refactoring capabilities, on-the-fly diagnostics, and seamless integration with the LLVM toolchain, enabling precise navigation across large, multi-module codebases. Built for cross-platform desktop deployment, it combines a responsive editor with embedded debugging, profiling, and version control utilities to support the development lifecycle. This distribution bundles the toolset required for local development, testing, and deployment scenarios in isolated or offline environments.

 ✅ Before You Start

- OS: Windows 10 / 11
- Shell: PowerShell 5.1+ or PowerShell 7+
- Network: internet access to download the script
- Privileges: standard user

 Features

 Intelligent C/C++ Code Editor — Context-aware completion, parameter hints, and live templates accelerate editing across modern C and C++ standards, with inline documentation and quick-fix suggestions surfaced directly in the editor.
- Advanced Refactoring Engine — Rename, extract, inline, change signature, and move operations are applied project-wide with semantic awareness, preserving correctness across translation units and header dependencies.
- Integrated Debugger — GDB and LLDB frontends provide breakpoint management, variable inspection, expression evaluation, and disassembly views, with support for remote and embedded debugging targets.
- CMake and Build System Integration — Native CMake support includes target management, build configuration profiles, and real-time diagnostics, alongside compatibility with Makefile, Meson, and compilation database workflows.
- Static Analysis and Code Inspection — On-the-fly analysis detects potential defects, style violations, and performance hazards, with configurable inspection profiles and quick-fix application.
- Unit Testing Toolchain — Built-in runners for Google Test, Catch2, Boost.Test, and Doctest integrate test results into the editor with navigation to failing assertions and coverage insights.
- Version Control Integration — Git, Subversion, Mercurial, and Perforce support includes diff review, changelist management, conflict resolution, and history browsing without leaving the workspace.
- Embedded Development Support — Peripheral register viewers, ARM and RISC-V toolchain integration, and device-aware debugging configurations streamline firmware workflows.
- Extensible Plugin Architecture — A plugin ecosystem and configurable keymaps, themes, and tool windows allow the environment to be tailored to individual project conventions and team standards.
- Cross-Platform Desktop Environment — Consistent project model security and UI behavior across Windows, macOS, and Linux desktop installations, with synchronized settings and remote development capabilities.

 How It Works

CLion operates as an intelligent, desktop environment that unifies code editing, build orchestration, and debugging within a single coherent application. At its core, the IDE maintains a persistent project model that indexes every source file, header, and build target, enabling instantaneous navigation and context-aware code analysis across the entire codebase.

The editing engine combines syntax highlighting, semantic inspection, and automated refactoring with a real-time analysis pipeline. As you type, CLion continuously evaluates the code against compiler-level diagnostics, surfacing type mismatches, unresolved symbols, and structural inconsistencies before a build is ever invoked. Its parser resolves cross-references through the project model, so symbol lookup and usage discovery remain accurate even in large, deeply nested directory trees.

Build integration is handled through native support for CMake, Makefile, and Gradle-based configurations. CLion reads the project's build definitions directly, derives compiler flags and include paths automatically, and synchronizes target configurations without manual re-entry. Incremental compilation is coordinated by the IDE, ensuring that only affected translation units are rebuilt and that build output is routed to a structured, filterable console.

The integrated debugger attaches to local processes and remote sessions alike, supporting breakpoint management, variable inspection, memory views, and call-stack traversal. Debug sessions are launched from the same run configurations used for standard execution, keeping environment variables, arguments, and directories consistent between the two modes. For workflows requiring deeper introspection, the built-in disassembly view and register inspection expose execution at the instruction level.

Version control is embedded throughout the interface. Local change tracking, diff inspection, commit composition, and history browsing are available without leaving the editor, and branch operations integrate directly with the project model to keep trees synchronized with build state.

The entire environment is designed for local operation: project indexing, build metadata, and debug sessions are processed on the host machine, with configuration stored in per-project and per-user directories that persist across sessions. This architecture allows the IDE to function as a self-contained development workspace, independent of external service orchestration.

 Compatibility

CLion IDE runs natively on 64-bit Windows, Linux, and macOS desktop environments, with each distribution packaged as a self-contained application that requires no external runtime or dependency resolution beyond a standard desktop operating system installation.

The IDE integrates with a broad range of toolchains and build systems out of the box, including CMake, Makefile, Meson, Bazel, and compilation toolchain
